meeting_header: Date: 2025-08-14 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~52 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Moretti (Redwood SE), Anna Park (Redwood Product), Rajiv Patel (HelixHealth), Sophie Lee (HelixHealth), Diego Ramirez (HelixHealth), Priya Nair (HelixHealth)
summary: SE-led Optimize walkthrough focusing on quantization profiles (INT8, FP8), how to pick profiles by workload, and concrete latency vs quality tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: Helix to send prompt corpus and SLOs; Redwood to share benchmark CSV and pilot config. Discussed fallback/rollout patterns, monitoring signals, and security/Private deployment notes.
topics: Optimize console tour: Q-profiles and profile suggestions
INT8 vs FP8 quality delta for chat and RAG
Latency SLOs, batching, and KV cache impacts
Rollout strategies: canary, auto-fallback, and A/B
Security/Private deployment implications for encrypted KVs and audit logs
transcript: 00:00 Maya: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off and Luca will drive the Optimize portion.
00:09 Rajiv: Hi, thanks. Quick note, we're joining from SF and London so if I duck out for a minute that is why.
00:18 Luca: Cool, I'll share my screen — show the Q-profiles UI, it's the page that recommends INT8/FP8 and mixed profiles per model. Just a sec...
00:30 Sophie: One thing we want to validate: our primary use is a chat assistant tied to clinical notes, latency SLO is 450ms p50 and 900ms p95, cost is big too — so where do we start?

00:45 Luca: Great. High-level: INT8 tends to win on cost, FP8 tends to preserve quality on generative tasks, but the console gives you an eval-first path. You can upload a prompt set and labeling to calculate quality deltas across profiles.
01:12 Diego: When you say FP8, are you talking about standard IEEE or vendor custom formats? We have some on-prem tensor cores that are picky.

01:25 Luca: Good question — we have three FP8 backends: a generic sim on CPU for estimates, an accelerator-specific kernel we flag in the profile, and a fallback path. We'll show the profile metadata in the demo. Sometimes the name is slightly different in the runtime logs — transcription sometimes shows "fpateight" in older runs, ignore that — ha.
01:48 Anna: We also want to understand the combinatorics: batch size, sequence length distributions, and KV cache hits — how much of the latency delta is actually network vs compute?

02:05 Luca: Right. In the Optimize console we surface token-level latency breakdowns — you can see model compute vs KV fetch vs network. For RAG, KV/cache warm hits can shave 30–60% off tail latency. We'll run a small benchmark now with a demo model and two Q-profiles.
02:28 Maya: Note, this session is demo-quality; numbers will be representative, we'll run a Helix-specific benchmark when Rajiv shares the prompt set.
02:40 [screen share noise; clicking]
03:01 Luca: Launching a 5k-token batch run, profile A = INT8-default, profile B = FP8-aggressive. Starting run...
03:15 Priya: Can you pause — how are you instrumenting the human eval? We use clinician labels for correctness and hallucination rates.
03:26 Luca: We support rubric-based scoring; you can plug in threshold rules or upload human labels. For demo I have a synthetic quality metric (QA accuracy) to show relative delta.
03:45 [typing sounds]
04:02 Luca: Initial results coming in: INT8 p50=160ms, p95=520ms; FP8 p50=210ms, p95=680ms. Cost per 1k tokens: INT8 ~$0.065, FP8 ~$0.11 — these numbers are synthetic, again —
04:28 Rajiv: Okay that gap looks significant. What's the observed quality delta on your QA metric?

04:36 Luca: On the synthetic QA set, INT8 accuracy=88.3%, FP8 accuracy=90.1% — so a ~1.8 point delta. For generative free text, we usually see slightly larger deltas on F1 and hallucination counts. But the Optimize console will show per-prompt deltas so you can find which prompts are brittle.
05:05 Sophie: The 1.8 points could be material for compliance-sensitive answers. Do you recommend mixed profiles where we run safety-critical prompts on FP8 and everything else INT8?

05:18 Luca: Yes. The console supports routing by prompt tag or by runtime classifier — you can run a quick classifier that decides which profile to hit, or use route-by-namespace where certain endpoints always use FP8.
05:34 Diego: How does rollout work? If we want to gradually shift traffic to INT8 we need automatic fallback if degradation is detected.

05:43 Luca: We have a canary rollout step and auto-fallback policies. You set guardrails: e.g., drop in quality >2% or hallucination increase triggers rollback. Those metrics can be tied to your eval set or to live SLOs via an alert threshold.
06:05 Maya: Quick pause — security question from Rajiv in chat: if we run Optimize in Private (VPC) does the console still get telemetry for suggestions?
06:16 Rajiv: (in chat) we need to know if any prompt content leaves customer network in Private mode

06:22 Anna: If you're in Private, Optimize suggestions can run using on-prem scoring workers — telemetry is limited to anonymized metrics by default, and you can opt into no-forwarding for raw prompts. We'll include details in the security pack.
06:40 Sophie: Good. Let's see the per-prompt delta — show us the prompt-level waterfall.

06:49 Luca: Switching to per-prompt diff view... here's a prompt where INT8 drops on hallucination — you can see token-level alignments where the softmax distribution gets noisier. The console highlights "hot prompts" where INT8 fails.
07:22 Priya: Can we threshold and automatically route those hot prompts to FP8? We don't want manual ops.
07:30 Luca: Yup, rule-based routing is in the UI. You can also do ML-based routing — small classifier trained on your labeled set. That classifier can run in-line and is cheap.
07:48 Rajiv: On the cost side, how do you show the tradeoffs? Our CFO wants a cost projection over expected monthly tokens.

07:58 Maya: The console has a cost estimator. We'll plug your monthly token estimate and the optimizer will suggest profiles to meet a cost target while respecting quality constraints. We'll attach the estimator CSV to the follow-up.
08:15 Diego: Does quantization affect embedding quality? We rely on embeddings for retrieval (RAG).

08:24 Luca: Generally embeddings are more robust to quantization, but extremes can degrade recall slightly. For retrieval we often recommend INT8 for the embedder and reserve FP8 for generative overlay. The Optimize UI lets you run recall/R-precision evals across profiles.
09:00 Sophie: Are there any workloads where INT8 unexpectedly regresses a lot?

09:07 Luca: Long-form code or math tends to be more brittle. Also models with heavy attention cross-talk sometimes need FP8. That's why we recommend a holdout of failure modes and run stress tests in the console.
09:30 [laughter]
09:35 Rajiv: You mentioned batch size earlier — show the batch-sweep tool. We care about p95 at 900ms — batch tuning might help cost but hurt tail latency.

09:50 Luca: Opening the batch sweep panel. Here you can try multiple batch sizes and concurrency and see latency percentiles. Note the KV cache warm/hits dramatically change the shape — when cache hit rate is 80% p95 drops a lot.
10:12 Priya: Can the Optimize engine suggest a combined profile that uses INT8 with FP8 for select layers (mixed quant)?

10:21 Luca: We have a mixed-precision hint called "layer-selective" that pins certain critical layers to FP8; Optimize recommends layer candidates based on gradient-free sensitivity analysis. It's experimental but available in Dedicated and Private.
10:45 Rajiv: For Private deployment, will the layer pins work with our on-prem GPUs? We use a mix of A100s and older V100s.

10:55 Luca: There's a compatibility matrix. V100s often need particular kernels; the console flags unsupported combos and suggests nearest compatible profile. We'll include that matrix in the follow-up.
11:15 Sophie: Can you walk through a short A/B test config to measure production impact?

11:23 Luca: Yes. In routes -> rollouts you configure a canary percent, attach an eval set, and tie metrics. For example: 10% traffic INT8 for 1 day, monitor QA accuracy and p95. If pass, ramp to 50% etc. If fail, rollback.
12:01 [silence as screen shared]

12:20 Luca: One more demo item: automatic retraining of the routing classifier. If routes mis-classify hot prompts, the system can flag them and add to retrain queue. Useful to reduce manual labeling.
12:42 Rajiv: How do you protect PII during console evals? Our prompts have PHI (protected health info).

12:52 Anna: For PHI we recommend Private deployment with KMS and HSM integration. Optimize supports anonymization hooks and you can configure a redaction pipeline prior to sending data to scoring workers. We'll provide details in the security packet.
13:18 Sophie: Can we get a short example of the JSON policy for auto-fallback? We want to show legal the escape hatch.
13:28 Luca: I'll paste one into the chat. Example: {"metric": "QA_accuracy", "threshold": 0.02, "action": "rollback"}. The UI builds this visually too. (Note: transcript sometimes munges braces.)
13:58 [chat paste noise]
14:10 Maya: Quick Q from Diego — monitoring: what dashboards are available right away vs via long-term retention add-on?
14:19 Luca: Out of the box you get 30 days of request-level traces, token-level cost and latency breakdowns. Longer retention and advanced analytics are an add-on.
14:34 Diego: Ok. Anything else we should discuss for the pilot?
14:39 Rajiv: Timeline: we'd like a pilot that runs 1 week to collect metrics against our prompts. Can Redwood spin up Dedicated trial capacity?
14:50 Maya: Yes, we have a short dedicated trial program. I'll include pricing and trial terms in the follow-up. We can also do a Private eval if security requires it.
15:06 Sophie: And what happens on a burst above capacity? We can't degrade to 10x latency during business hours.

15:14 Luca: Smart routing can fallback to a cheaper FP8 variant in a different region or degrade gracefully to a smaller model that maintains correctness. We also support autoscaling policies tuned to latency targets.
15:28 Priya: Any gotchas we should watch for in our first run? We have a lot of short chat turns (~8 tokens avg) but occasional long attachments (2k tokens).

15:40 Luca: Watch for tail effects from occasional long context. Optimize lets you define a long-tail rule: long contexts route to a different profile or are rate-limited. Also consider prefix/KV caching to reduce cost on repeated contexts.
16:02 Rajiv: Can you show the exportable CSV of per-prompt diffs? We'll want that for our compliance team.
16:10 Luca: Exporting now... done. Link in chat: drive.redwood/benchmarks/heli-2025-08-14.csv
16:22 Sophie: I see some prompts with >5% drop in QA for INT8 — those will be our initial FP8 bucket.
16:31 Maya: Great, next step is Helix to share full prompt corpus and target SLOs; Redwood will run a Helix-specific benchmark and propose pilot config and pricing.
16:45 Rajiv: Anything else on compliance? We need SOC2 evidence for logging of model changes during pilot.
16:53 Anna: We'll include a packaged SOC2 excerpt showing audit logs and model versioning; also a short runbook for emergency rollback.
17:08 Sophie: Who should I loop in on legal?
17:12 Rajiv: Please loop legal (name withheld) and our procurement contact — we'll send contact details after this call.
17:25 Maya: Perfect. I'll follow-up with the benchmark CSV, the cost estimator, the Private compatibility matrix, and a proposed pilot SOW.
17:39 Diego: One offline item — will you provide a small script to bucket token lengths? That'll speed up our token distribution share.
17:48 Luca: Yes, I'll add a tiny python snippet in the follow-up. It uses the tokenizer to produce a histogram.
18:00 [wrap up]

18:05 Maya: Thanks everyone. Recap: Helix sends prompt corpus + SLOs; Redwood runs pilot bench and returns config and pricing. Expect follow-up by 2025-08-20. We'll set up the pilot for week of 2025-08-25.
18:22 Rajiv: Thanks all, appreciate it.
18:27 [call ends]
52:00 (recording length marker)
